items.title: Al Chez interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, February 13, 2019
items.q: I called Shaffer up... 'if you want to add a trumpet full time I won't go on the road anymore.' ... 'the kid stays.' ... to be the trumpet player on the show.

ctx.x: So did you have like a run through in the afternoon if you were going to have musical guests?

We usually got there at like 3:45 and then we would do rehearsal. We would get a script and it would say Alec Baldwin is the first guest. And they’d say okay. We would rehearse for the show and our — I did it for 17 years, Willie did it for 30 years, Paul was 30 years, Anton — I think it was Steve Jordan then Anton, so Anton was 20 something years. These guys don’t want to rehearse. You know what I mean? So our rehearsals ran seven to nine minutes. That’s how long the rehearsal was every day. So you had a script…
No one wrote out a chart in other words.

items.title: Paul Shaffer interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 24, 2023
items.q: You know I was able to talk to Al Chez who was on the band for a while.

ctx.x: Talking about Renee Fleming and you —

Oh yeah, yeah, yeah, she mentioned it. She says, “I’ve got a tape of you singing those ten songs in full voice whatever that means. To me it was just really a day’s work but then Tom was able to take my tape and arrange it and he did a beautiful job and we brought in special — you know he asked for a bassoon I think and an oboe. New York is the kind of © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

place where you just make one call and they’re there at 10 AM. Renee Fleming came into my dressing room, we had our little woodwind ensemble Chez — I don’t know if Chez was with us on that day or not anymore, but parts for everybody thanks to Tom, who stayed up all night writing these things, and then Renee making sure that she could time them right. Because it’s got to be camera goes back to Dave, he says, “Number seven” bang back to Renee who is now singing it. So really when he’s saying “Number seven” I’m…
